question: Let $C$ be a circle of area $A$ with centre at $O$. Let $P$ be a moving point such that its distance from $O$ is always twice the length of a tangent drawn from $P$ to the circle. Then the point $P$ must move along

options.A: the sides of a square centred at $O$, with area $\frac43A$.
options.B: the sides of an equilateral triangle centred at $O$, with area $4A$.
options.C: a circle centred at $O$, with area $\frac43A$.
options.D: a circle centred at $O$, with area $4A.
